issues.legal_issue: Compensation for increased construction costs must account for benefits received from property appreciation, interest already paid, and the consumer’s delay in beginning construction.
material_facts: Physical possession of an allotted plot was delayed until 2000, although it was due in 1989.
The consumer had paid the plot price and had received interest on the amount deposited.
The plot increased in value during the period before possession was delivered.
The consumer did not begin construction until 2006, and the State Commission found that construction had been delayed to obtain higher compensation.
The State Commission awarded compensation for increased construction costs, which the National Commission confirmed.
issues.conclusion: The award of compensation for increased construction costs was excessive and unreasonable because it failed to account for the increase in the plot’s value, the interest already paid, and the consumer’s delay in commencing construction. Interest was sufficient compensation for the loss caused by delayed possession, so the construction-cost compensation award was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 14(1)(d) of the Consumer Protection Act, 1986, compensation requires proof of loss or injury caused by the opposite party’s negligence, and the amount must be fair, reasonable, and commensurate with that loss or injury after considering all relevant factors. Charan Singh v. Healing Touch Hospital and Others, (2000) 7 SCC 668, holds that compensation depends on the facts of each case and must be assessed on accepted legal principles and with moderation. Ghaziabad Development Authority v. Balbir Singh, (2004) 4 SCC 65, holds that compensation where possession is delivered must account for the benefit of the property’s increased value and be determined by examining the actual harassment or loss in the particular case.

rule.if: consumer_compensation_appeal and delayed_physical_possession and plot_value_appreciated and interest_already_paid and construction_delayed_for_higher_compensation and construction_cost_compensation_awarded

predicates.consumer_compensation_appeal: The matter is an appeal concerning a consumer forum’s compensation award.
predicates.delayed_physical_possession: The service provider delivered physical possession later than it was required to.
predicates.plot_value_appreciated: The property increased in value during the period before possession was delivered.
predicates.interest_already_paid: The consumer had already received interest on the amount deposited.
predicates.construction_delayed_for_higher_compensa: The consumer delayed beginning construction after receiving possession, and the forum found the delay was intended to obtain higher compensation.
predicates.construction_cost_compensation_awarded: The consumer forum awarded compensation for increased construction costs.

issues.definition: When a consumer compensation appeal concerns delayed possession, the property appreciated in value, interest was already paid, construction was delayed to obtain higher compensation, and construction-cost compensation was awarded, that compensation is unwarranted.
